## Documentation {#documentation}

- **`StreamPath` docs no longer call it lazy where the source is read at once** ([#1290](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1290)). The cheat sheet and home page describe sequences you can run more than once, and `toStreamPath` says the non-null focuses are collected into a list when it is called.
- **The StreamPath docs say when the source is read** ([#1278](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1278)). `Path.stream` reads its whole stream when it is called, so the stream must be finite. `Path.streamIterate`, `StreamPath.generate` and `StreamPath.fromSupplier` build a fresh stream each time the path runs, so `take` can limit an infinite one. See [Choosing the Right Streaming Tool](../monads/vstream.md#choosing-the-right-streaming-tool).
- **The Effect Paths glossary gains three entries** ([#1301](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1301)): `FreeApPath`, `FreePath` and `GenericPath`. Each gives a definition, its factories on `Path`, and its main operations. See [Effect Paths](../glossary/effect-paths.md#freeappath).
- **The Effect Paths glossary gains four more entries** ([#1258](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1258)): `ReaderPath`, `TrampolinePath`, `WithStatePath` and `WriterPath`. Each gives a definition, its factories on `Path`, its main operations and a link to its chapter page. See [Effect Paths](../glossary/effect-paths.md#readerpath).
- **Five examples keep one kind of Path and one error type through their chains.** Composition Patterns ran an `IOPath` step in an `EitherPath` chain, which throws when it runs; it now builds an `IOPath` chain. The Quickstart, a migration recipe and the `hkj-guide` and `hkj-spring` skills now name the chain's error type with a witness. See [Composition Patterns](../effect/composition.md#mistake-2-side-effects-in-map).
- **Generated Javadoc uses an article only before a type the processor chose** ([#1307](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1307)). A record, class, property or operation is named with none, as in `field of {@link Address}` and `Lifts the {@code Charge} operation`. A path or optic type keeps the article its name takes, as in `Creates an {@link AffinePath}`.
- **The `hkj-guide` skill turns guard clauses into `ensure`** ([#1338](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1338)). A new migration recipe replaces a run of `if (!ok) return Either.left(...)` checks with one `ensure` step for each, and the skill's Error Handling table lists `ensure`.
- **The `Profunctor` javadoc states its composition law correctly** ([#1362](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/pull/1362)). Two of its functions were swapped, so the law as written fails. It no longer says profunctors model the optics, which are van Laarhoven optics, and `Bifunctor`'s javadoc names `Function` as the only `Profunctor` instance. See [Profunctor](../functional/profunctor.md).

## Upgrading from 0.5.0 {#upgrading}

### Before you upgrade {#before-you-upgrade}

### What a running program can notice {#runtime-changes}

#### Core types {#runtime-core-types}

- **`Validated.map`, and `map2` to `map5` on its monad, throw `NullPointerException` when their function returns null** ([#1318](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1318)). They threw `KindUnwrapException`, so catching that, or `IllegalArgumentException`, around the call no longer catches it. See [Values, never null](../hkts/core-concepts.md#values-never-null).
- **`FunctionKindHelper.narrow` throws `KindUnwrapException`, as the other kind helpers do** ([#1318](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1318)). A null `Kind` threw `NullPointerException`, so catching that no longer catches it. Another type's `Kind` threw `IllegalArgumentException`, which `KindUnwrapException` extends, so catching that still does. See [When `narrow` throws](../hkts/core-concepts.md#when-narrow-throws).
- **A `Selective` of your own no longer runs the effects its condition skips** ([#1358](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/pull/1358)), unless its `select` is built from `ap`. The default `whenS` ran its effect on a false condition, and the default `ifS` ran both branches, so a failing effect's error could hide the condition's. Run any effect you relied on yourself. The library's own instances are unchanged.

#### Optics {#runtime-optics}

- **Of two withers for one getter, `@ImportOptics` sets through the capitalised spelling** ([#1148](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1148)): the lens for a class with both `withEMail` and `witheMail` beside `eMail()` set through whichever the class declared first. It now sets through `withEMail`, and a note names `witheMail`, which a spec interface's `@Wither` can choose.
- **An optic interpreter that wraps each result in `Free.pure` skips the operation's continuation** ([#1154](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1154)): a program from `OpticPrograms` runs as before, but a function mapped onto an `OpticOp`, through `OpticOpFunctor` or `Free.translate`, is not applied. Hand the result to `op.k()` and return what it gives.

#### Effect Paths {#runtime-effect-paths}

- **A `ValidationPath` keeps its own semigroup through a step** ([#1314](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1314)): the result of `via`, `then`, `recoverWith` and `orElse` accumulated with the step's semigroup, and now accumulates with the receiver's. After `mapError`, whose placeholder semigroup throws, a later accumulation now throws even past a step that had a semigroup; use `mapErrorWith` instead.
- **An `EitherOrBothPath` keeps its own semigroup through a recovery** ([#1314](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1314)): the result of `recoverWith` and `orElse` accumulated with the recovery's semigroup, and now accumulates with the receiver's, as `via` and `then` already did.
- **`mapError` on `MaybePath`, `TryPath` and `CompletableFuturePath` applies the mapper** ([#1332](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1332)): it used to hand back the same path, and it never called the mapper. A failure now runs the mapper, and `recover` sees that error. `MaybePath` and `TryPath` return an `EitherPath`. `CompletableFuturePath` returns a `VResultPath`. `mapException` still stays a `TryPath`.

### What stops a build that compiled {#build-changes}

| Area | Now fails the build | Do this | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| Effect Paths | A chain step of another kind of Path, or with an error, environment, state, log or witness type the chain does not carry | Convert the step, map its error, or type the chain on the wider error where it starts, as [Common Compiler Errors](../effect/compiler_errors.md) shows | [#1314](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1314) |
| Effect Paths | Code that names a capability type with its old arguments, such as `Effectful<A>`, or a `PathProvider` returning `Chainable<A>` | Write `Effectful<?, A>`, or `<P, A> Effectful<P, A>` in a helper that chains. The `AddPathFamily` recipe writes the first | [#1314](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1314) |
| Effect Paths | A chain whose receiver is typed with a wildcard error, such as `EitherPath<? extends AppError, String>` | Widen it first, as in `p.<AppError>mapError(e -> e).via(...)`, or declare it as `EitherPath<AppError, String>` | [#1314](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1314) |
| Effect Paths | A pattern or cast from a capability type to a concrete Path, such as `case MaybePath<String> m` on a `Chainable<?, String>`; a cast is unchecked, so it fails under `-Werror` | Match from `Composable<String>`, or build the concrete Path directly | [#1314](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1314) |
| Effect Paths | A step after `mapError` on a `MaybePath`, `TryPath` or `CompletableFuturePath` that returns the Path it started from | Return an `EitherPath` from the step (a `VResultPath` after a `CompletableFuturePath`), or use `recover` or `mapException` before changing the error type | [#1332](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1332) |
| Optics | An optic interpreter or other code of your own that names an `OpticOp` record: a pattern or type such as `OpticOp.Get<?, ?>` or `OpticOp.Set<S, A>`, or a constructor call such as `new OpticOp.Get<>(source, getter)` | Add the third type argument, as in `OpticOp.Get<?, ?, ?>`, and pass a continuation, `Function.identity()`, to a constructor. Hand each result to `op.k()` and return what it gives, in place of `Free.pure(result)` | [#1154](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1154) |
| Build and tooling | Build logic that reads the `hkjInstallSkills` task's `outputDir` as a `Path` | Read `outputDir.get().asFile.toPath()`, which names the same directory | [#1374](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1374) |

# v0.5.0 (26 October 2026) {#v050-26-october-2026}

[v0.5.0 on GitHub](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/releases/tag/v0.5.0)

This release makes the optics generated for a record easier to reach and safer to hold. Navigators are on by default, so `OrderFocus.lines().quantity()` chains through a list from a bare `@GenerateFocus`, and every optic and Focus path takes a `@Nullable` focus. The core types now refuse null as a success, as an error and as a lazy value, so a `null` fails where it is made rather than where it is read. Resources are released exactly once, whatever stops the work. Every API deprecated for removal in 0.5.0 is gone, and `MigrateDeprecationsTo0_5_0` migrates most calls.

~~~admonish info title="At a glance"
- **Navigators are on by default, and a navigator is a path.** `UserFocus.address().street()` and `OrderFocus.lines().quantity()` work with a bare `@GenerateFocus`, and the navigator goes wherever a path goes.
- **Optics over a nullable field pass a nullness checker.** Every optic and Focus path type takes a `@Nullable` focus, and a bridge into an Effect Path can say what a null focus becomes.
- **No success, error or lazy value is null.** `Either`, `Try`, `IO`, `VTask`, `VStream` and every Path over them refuse null as a success, an error or a lazy value, and `Unit` stands for a step with nothing to return.
- **Resources are released exactly once.** A `VStream`, a `Resource`, a `bracket` and a `Scope` clean up whatever stops them: an early `take`, a failure, a timeout or a cancellation.
- **Optics cost less.** A read through a traversal no longer rebuilds what it reads, a fold stops at its answer, and a Focus path rebuilds a 100,000-element list in about a millisecond.
- **Every API deprecated for removal in 0.5.0 is gone.** `MigrateDeprecationsTo0_5_0` migrates most calls, and the build table gives the fix for the rest. A Focus path's untyped shortcuts are deprecated for removal in 0.6.0, and `MigrateDeprecationsTo0_6_0` replaces them.
- **The Optics chapter is rewritten.** It reads in order from a first nested update to a PATCH, on one order service, with every example compiled and checked.
- **Some changes alter what a running program does.** Many others stop the build, so read [Upgrading from 0.4.11](#upgrading) first.
~~~

---

## Mapping {#mapping}

### Generic specs {#generic-specs}

- **A bounded generic spec covers only what its bound admits** ([#1118](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1118)). A spec over `Page<T>` with `T extends Number` covered a `Page<String>` field and broke the generated code. That field now reports no usable source, naming the bound, or nests through a spec for `Page<String>` declared beside it. See [A bounded spec covers only what its bounds admit](../mapping/rules.md#generic-spec-bounds).
- **A generic spec over an array of its parameter leaves a primitive array alone** ([#1091](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1091)). No type argument is a primitive, so a spec over `Page<T[]>` no longer covers a `Page<int[]>` field, which crashed the processor or failed in generated code. The field reports no usable source instead. See [The boundaries of a generic spec](../mapping/rules.md#generic-boundaries).
- **An element-mapped spec nests where a type argument passes through unconverted** ([#1122](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1122)). A spec over `TaggedPage<T, X>` whose leaf converts only the elements broke the generated code wherever it nested, since no leaf names `X`. The generated call now spells out its type arguments, keeping a `@Nullable` the records declare. See [How an element-mapped spec nests](../mapping/rules.md#element-mapped-nesting).
- **A merge fills a component through a generic spec** ([#1123](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1123)). A threaded spec such as `PageMapping<T>` now fills a merge as it nests in a mapping. An element-mapped spec is not supported yet, and the merge says so, offering the leaf that builds it. See [How a merge fills](../mapping/rules.md#how-a-merge-fills).
- **The most specific of several specs for a pair maps it** ([#1123](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1123)). `TagPageMapping` beside `PageMapping<T>`, or `PageMapping<T>` beside `CodecPageMapping<T, TDto>`, made a field ambiguous. The more specific now maps it, and a compiler note names a dependency's spec it displaced. See [The most specific spec for a pair is used](../mapping/rules.md#generic-spec-precedence).

### Beans, builders and codecs {#beans-builders-codecs}

- **More Lombok `@Singular` collections map** ([#1110](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1110)). A build-only collection whose name has a capital second letter, such as `eMails`, is written whole, whichever capitalisation Lombok gives its clear method. So is one of an unbounded wildcard, or a Guava `ImmutableTable`. An `Iterable` property without type arguments is no longer taken for one. See [A Lombok `@Singular` collection](../mapping/rules.md#singular-collections).
- **A method that only starts like an accessor is never read as one** ([#1128](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1128)). A name that runs on in lower case after its `get`, `is` or `set` prefix is a word, while `geteMail()` stays the JavaBeans getter of `eMail`. So `getaway()` no longer reads `away`, and a builder's `settings(String)` writes `settings`. See [How a bean is read and written](../mapping/rules.md#how-a-bean-is-read-and-written).
- **A word a component needs is refused, with the accessor to write** ([#1128](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1128)). A bean's `getx()` and `setx(int)`, with no accessor of `x` beside them, used to be read as `x`. The error now offers `getX()` and `setX(int)`, or an `@Unmapped` marker. See [A method that only starts like an accessor](../mapping/rules.md#word-accessors).
- **A builder with both `name(...)` and `setName(...)` maps** ([#1128](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1128)): the two were taken for rival overloads, which javac never weighs against each other, and the property was refused. `name(...)` writes it. See [How a bean is read and written](../mapping/rules.md#how-a-bean-is-read-and-written).
- **The processor names what an accessor-style leaf or marker meant** ([#907](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/907)): a leaf written `getEmail()` for the component `email` now draws `Did you mean 'email()'?`, as a near misspelling already did. An `@Unmapped` or `@ReadOnly` marker named after its accessor, `setStamp()` or `getId()`, draws the property the same way. See [Compiler Messages](../mapping/compiler_errors.md#leaf-names-no-component).
- **A date codec refuses a formatter that cannot parse what it writes** ([#1144](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1144)): `StandardCodecs.localDate(formatter)` and `offsetDateTime(formatter)` throw `IllegalArgumentException` when built over one, such as a pattern with no year. Such a codec used to reject every input while quoting a sample it rejected itself. See [Canonical forms only](../mapping/codecs.md#canonical-forms-only).
- **A misspelt `@MapKey` value suggests the component's bare name** ([#1112](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1112)). The hint now offers `byOwner` rather than `byOwner()`, so it can be used as the annotation's value. Hints that name methods keep their parentheses.

---

## Optics {#optics}

### Navigators by default {#navigators}

- **`@GenerateFocus` generates navigators by default, and a navigator is a path** ([#1033](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1033)). `UserFocus.address().street()` works on a bare annotation, and `generateNavigators = false` turns navigators off. A navigator can be held as a `FocusPath` or passed to an Effect Path's `focus`, and every path method works on it. See [Fluent navigation with generated navigators](../optics/focus_navigation.md#fluent-navigation-with-generated-navigators).
- **`OrderFocus.lines().quantity()` chains with no `.via(...)`** ([#1103](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1103)). A `List`, `Set`, `Collection`, `Optional` or `Maybe` of records gets a navigator, and so does one nested in another, such as `List<Optional<LineItem>>`, or a `Kind` the processor traverses. The navigator is the path the method returned before, so code that declares that path type still compiles. See [Which fields get a navigator](../optics/focus_navigation.md#which-fields-get-a-navigator).
- **`OrderHistoryFocus.orders().customer().email()` keeps navigating after a hop that widens the path** ([#1214](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1214)). Each navigator nests a form for each wider path type, `AffineForm` and `TraversalForm`, and a widening hop into a record field returns it. A record that writes `generateNavigators = true` is told when a form is left out. See [Which fields get a navigator](../optics/focus_navigation.md#which-fields-get-a-navigator).
- **A navigator steps into a container only where the record widens it** ([#1033](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1033)). A `Map`, an array or a third-party collection of `@GenerateFocus` records gets a navigator under `widenCollections = true`, or when the new `widenFields` names the field. So turning navigators on never changes what a field's method focuses on. See [The `ZERO_OR_MORE` Asymmetry](../optics/focus_containers.md#the-zero_or_more-asymmetry-and-widencollections).
- **A navigator reaches into a generic record** ([#739](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/739), [#1061](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1061)): a field such as `Revision<EmailAddress> email` gets a navigator instantiated with its type arguments, so `ContactHistoryFocus.email().current()` chains. Where a field gets no navigator, as one given a wildcard does, its note names the path its method returns. See [A target with type parameters](../optics/focus_navigation.md#a-target-with-type-parameters).
- **A field named like a path method is handled at the declaration** ([#1033](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1033)). A navigator never reaches a field such as `last`, since `name().last()` would call `FocusPath.last()`. The field reaching such a record keeps its plain path, with a note, or is refused under `generateNavigators = true`. Fields named `get`, `set` and `count` navigate. See [A field named like a path method](../optics/focus_navigation.md#a-field-named-like-a-path-method).
- **Fields such as `items` and `Items` keep one navigator between them** ([#1259](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1259)). Where both would have a navigator, their classes would share a name, so the first in declaration order keeps it. The later one keeps its plain path, with a note, or is refused where the record writes `generateNavigators = true`. See [Two fields with one navigator name](../optics/focus_navigation.md#two-fields-with-one-navigator-name).
- **`@GenerateFocus` checks the names in `includeFields`, `excludeFields` and `widenFields`** ([#1104](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1104)). A name that matches no component is an error at the value, offering the component meant, such as `positions` for `"postions"`. A list the record never reads warns, as does a `widenFields` name whose field cannot widen. See [Compiler Messages](../optics/compiler_errors.md#generatefocus-field-list-unknown-name).
- **A `@GenerateFocus` setting that names a constant javac cannot resolve leaves only javac's error** ([#1104](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1104)), such as `includeFields = Names.MISSING`. The processor stopped with an exception, which hid that error.
- **`@GenerateFocus` warns of an `includeFields` name whose field has no navigator** ([#1181](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1181), [#1201](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1201), [#1207](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1207)). Naming only a `String` field, say, left every field without a navigator, and nothing said why. The warning says why and offers a fix: another field to name, a record to annotate, a container to widen, or `includeFields` to remove, with navigators off. See [Compiler Messages](../optics/compiler_errors.md#generatefocus-includefields-no-navigator).
- **`@GenerateFocus` reports a `TraversableGenerator` priority tie once** ([#1081](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1081)): the warning lands on the component that reaches the tied type, however many navigators reach it. It used to repeat for each one. See [Compiler Messages](../optics/compiler_errors.md#multiple-traversablegenerator-spi-providers-with-equal-priority-n-support-type-x-a-warning).

### Optics and null {#optics-and-null}

- **Optics over a nullable field pass a nullness checker** ([#767](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/767), [#1017](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1017)): every optic and Focus path type, and `Kind`, takes a nullable type, so the lens generated for a `@Nullable` component checks under JSpecify. A bridge into an effect type can say what a null focus becomes, as `toEitherPath(source, error)` does. See [A focus that may be null](../optics/focus_effects.md#a-focus-that-may-be-null).
- **`nullable()` keeps the focus type** ([#1017](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1017)): `FocusPath.nullable()` and `AffinePath.nullable()` return the focus type without its null, so a chained `focus(path.nullable(), error)` or a `var` infers it where it inferred `Object`. A call written `path.<String>nullable()` still compiles. See [`.nullable()`: Handle Null Values](../optics/focus_navigation.md#nullable-handle-null-values).
- **A Focus path passes over a null it would step into** ([#1062](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1062)). A `@Nullable` `List`, `Optional`, `Either` or other container now widens through `.nullable()` first, so its path is empty when the container is null, where it threw `NullPointerException`. A navigator into `Map<String, @Nullable Address>` reads the other elements and leaves a null one in place. See [Where a `@Nullable` counts](../optics/focus_navigation.md#where-a-nullable-counts).
- **`modifyAllEither`, `modifyAllValidated` and `modifyAllMaybe` keep a null element their traversal passes over** ([#1065](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1065)): over `filtered` or a prism that leaves a null element alone, `modifyAllValidated` threw and `modifyAllMaybe` gave `Nothing`. Each now keeps the null, and still rebuilds nothing once a step fails. So do `OpticOps`' validating modifiers. See [`modifyAllEither`: First Error Only](../optics/optics_extensions.md#modifyalleither-first-error-only).

### The containers a Focus path widens {#focus-containers}

- **A `Maybe` component's Focus path reads and writes its `Just` value** ([#757](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/757)): `@GenerateFocus` now widens a `Maybe` field, and one nested in another container such as `List<Maybe<A>>`, through `.some(Affines.just())`. It used the `Optional`-only `.some()`, so the first read or write threw `ClassCastException`. See [Supported Container Types](../optics/focus_containers.md#supported-container-types).
- **A raw or wildcard `Maybe`, `Set` or `Collection` component widens, as a `List` does** ([#1251](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1251)). `Set<? extends Widget>` widens to a `TraversalPath` onto `Widget`. In 0.4.11 such a `Set` or `Collection` was rejected at the declaration, and such a `Maybe` threw `ClassCastException` on first use. See [Supported Container Types](../optics/focus_containers.md#supported-container-types).
- **`@GenerateFocus` widens an array, as the Focus pages say** ([#1062](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1062)). Under `widenCollections = true`, a `String[]` or other array of a reference type is a `TraversalPath` over its elements, and an array of `@GenerateFocus` records gets a navigator over them. A primitive array stays a plain path. See [Supported Container Types](../optics/focus_containers.md#supported-container-types).
- **A Focus path through a custom container whose generator names no optic stops at the container** ([#1059](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1059)), as if no generator supported it. It used to widen through the `Optional`-only `.some()` or the `List`-only `.each()`, and threw `ClassCastException` on first use for other containers. The generator still serves `@GenerateTraversals` and `@ImportOptics`. See [Registering your own container type](../optics/focus_containers.md#the-fine-print-registering-your-own-container-type).
- **A Focus path's untyped shortcuts are deprecated for removal in 0.6.0** ([#1105](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1105)). `each()`, `some()`, `at(index)` and the others compile on any focus, then throw `ClassCastException` on the wrong one. Each typed form, such as `each(EachInstances.listEach())`, reads the element type from the path and does not compile on another focus. See [Deprecated for removal in 0.6.0](#deprecated).
- **`EachIndexed` is the one way to an indexed traversal from an `Each`** ([#1261](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1261)): `Each.eachWithIndex()`, deprecated since 0.4.7, is removed. It let the caller choose the index type, so a wrong one compiled, then threw `ClassCastException`. `indexedTraversal()` fixes the index type in its signature. See [Using Indexed Traversal](../optics/each_typeclass.md#using-indexed-traversal).

### Composition and cost {#composition-and-cost}

- **Any two of `Iso`, `Lens`, `Prism`, `Affine` and `Traversal` compose directly with `andThen`** ([#1021](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/pull/1021)). An `Iso` followed by a `Traversal` now returns a `Traversal`, and so does a `Traversal` followed by an `Affine` or an `Iso`, with no `asTraversal()` first. The composition table is read from the overloads, so it always matches the library. See [Composition Rules Table](../optics/composition_rules.md#composition-rules-table).
- **A read through a traversal no longer rebuilds what it reads** ([#1056](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/pull/1056)). `Traversals.getAll`, a `TraversalPath`'s reads, the indexed reads and `IxedInstances.get` read each focus as `asFold()` does, so reading a list or map through an optic no longer builds a new one. A prism or affine that matches builds nothing it throws away. See [What reads cost](../optics/production_readiness.md#read-cost).
- **A fold's query stops at its answer** ([#1056](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/pull/1056)). `preview`, `find`, `exists`, `all` and `isEmpty` on `Fold`, `TraversalPath` and `IndexedFold` visit no focus after the one that settles them, so `exists` over a long list returns at its first match. A path from `traced` still reads every focus, so its observer sees them all. See [What reads cost](../optics/production_readiness.md#read-cost).
- **A Focus path steps into a `List` in time proportional to the list** ([#1063](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1063)). Its `.each(EachInstances.listEach())`, which every generated `List` path uses, now rebuilds the list once instead of copying it at every element. On 100,000 elements that took several seconds, and now takes about a millisecond. `EachInstances.arrayEach()` rebuilds an array the same way. See [Traversal allocation](../optics/production_readiness.md#traversal-allocation).
- **A map written through an optic keeps its source's order** ([#1022](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/pull/1022)): every optic that writes a `Map`, from `Traversals.forMapValues` to `AtInstances.mapAt` and `Setter.forMapValues`, hands back a map in the source's iteration order. An updated key keeps its place and a new key goes at the end. See [Persistent and Third-Party Maps](../optics/common_data_structure_traversals.md#persistent-and-third-party-maps-formapvaluescollecting).
- **`modifyWhen` and `branch` on a `Traversal` call only the function their predicate picks** ([#1026](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/pull/1026)). Each element is now tested first, so a function may assume the condition that guards it, and an expensive one runs only where it is needed. `Lens.modifyWhen`, `modifyBranch` and `setIf` test first too. See [Complete, Runnable Example](../optics/composing_optics.md#complete-runnable-example).
- **`Setter.forList` and `Setter.forMapValues` give the same result on every run** ([#1018](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1018)): each time the effect from `modifyF` runs, it builds its own list or map. So an `IO` gives an equal value on every run, and the `List` applicative gives every combination of choices. `Traversals.traverseMapValues` does the same for an empty map. See [Sequencing Effects in Collections](../optics/setters.md#sequencing-effects-in-collections).

### Copy strategies, Lombok and protobuf builders {#copy-strategies}

- **`@ViaBuilder` rebuilds through Lombok's `@SuperBuilder(toBuilder = true)`** ([#1110](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1110)). Its `toBuilder()` hands back a builder typed with wildcards, `PetBuilder<?, ?>`, whose setter and `build()` the processor now follows as javac does. So does a hand-written builder handed back with wildcards, where a step returns one of its own type parameters. See [Non-Standard Naming](../optics/copy_strategies.md#non-standard-naming).
- **More `@ViaBuilder` chains are checked at the spec** ([#1110](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1110)). A spec over `Node<?>` whose `toBuilder()` returns a type parameter of `Node` builds. A builder bounded by more than one type is checked too, and a chain that cannot compile is refused at the spec rather than in the generated file. See [the chain the lens rebuilds through](../optics/compiler_errors.md#viabuilder-the-chain-the-lens-rebuilds-through).
- **A `@ViaBuilder` lens replaces a collection its builder would add to** ([#1110](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1110)). For a Lombok `@Singular List<String> tags`, or a protobuf-java message's `addAllTags` or `putAllPoints`, the generated lens first calls the `clearTags()` or `clearPoints()` written beside it, so the lens laws hold. That covers `@Builder` and `@SuperBuilder`, with or without a lower-case `setterPrefix`. See [Non-Standard Naming](../optics/copy_strategies.md#non-standard-naming).
- **A `@Wither` that returns its class's own type parameter works on a source written with a wildcard** ([#1110](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1110)): `S withName(String)` on a `Shape<S extends Shape<S>>` rebuilds a `Shape<?>`. See [Copy Strategies](../optics/copy_strategies.md#wither-types-with-withx-methods).
- **A spec's diagnostics never offer a deprecated method** ([#1110](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1110)). Following one failed a build under `-Werror` in the generated file. A lens named after a protobuf repeated or map field is offered `getTagsList()` or `getPointsMap()`, never the deprecated `getPoints()`. See [the missing accessor](../optics/compiler_errors.md#-has-no-method--for-the-generated-lens-to-read-the-value-it-focuses).
- **The processor suggests methods spelt the way each copy strategy calls them** ([#907](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/907)). A getter written `name` against a bean's `getName()` now draws `Did you mean 'getName'?`, and `getActive` draws `'isActive'`. A setter or wither is offered in the convention its strategy needs: a builder's `setName` or `name`, a bean's `setName`, `@Wither`'s `withName`. See [Compiler Messages](../optics/compiler_errors.md#-has-no-method--for-the-generated-lens-to-read-the-value-it-focuses).
- **`@ViaConstructor` holds its order to the constructor** ([#906](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/906)). An order that passes a value where the constructor's parameter names say another belongs, or that no constructor takes, is now refused at the spec method. Leave `parameterOrder` out and it is read from those names. See [`@ViaConstructor`: constructor-only value types](../optics/copy_strategies.md#viaconstructor-constructor-only-value-types).
- **A `@ViaConstructor` order that leaves a value out says so** ([#1067](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1067)). A written order that rebuilds through a shorter constructor now warns, naming the values longer constructors take. `@SuppressWarnings("shorter-constructor")` keeps quiet a constructor that works the value out on purpose. A variable-arity constructor is held to its parameter names too. See [the warning's entry](../optics/compiler_errors.md#viaconstructor-shorter-constructor).
- **A `@ViaCopyAndSet` lens keeps what its `withX` setter returns** ([#1108](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1108)). A `withTitle` setter had its new value dropped. The lens now hands back what it returns where every method of that name the new value can be passed to returns the source type. One it cannot keep warns, unless the lens method is annotated `@SuppressWarnings("dropped-result")`. See [`@ViaCopyAndSet`](../optics/copy_strategies.md#viacopyandset-legacy-types-with-a-copy-constructor-and-setters).
- **`@ImportOptics` takes no word for a wither** ([#1128](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1128)). A name that runs on in lower case after `with` is a word, so a `withdraw(long)` beside `getDraw()`, which gave a `draw` lens that added to `draw` rather than setting it, now gives none. A `with2D(int)` beside `get2D()` no longer stops the processor. See [Wither Classes to Lenses](../optics/importing_optics.md#wither-classes-to-lenses).
- **A spec lens that would read or rebuild unchecked through a raw type is refused at the spec method** ([#905](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/905)). A raw accessor read as `List<String>`, or a setter called through a raw builder, left an unchecked operation in generated code, which failed a build under `-Xlint:unchecked -Werror`. The error names the member at fault. See [Compiler Errors](../optics/compiler_errors.md#spec-unchecked-conversion).

### Prisms and `@InstanceOf` {#prisms}

- **A prism onto an inner class of a generic class compiles under `-Werror`** ([#886](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/886)): a `Dot` declared inside `class Outlines<X>` gets `Prism<Outlines.Outline, Outlines<?>.Dot>`, from `@GeneratePrisms`, `@ImportOptics` and an `@InstanceOf` spec method. A generic inner class gets a prism too, where `@InstanceOf` refused one. See [Generating the Prisms](../optics/prisms.md#step-1-generating-the-prisms) and [Parameterised Targets](../optics/optics_spec_interfaces.md#parameterised-targets).
- **`@InstanceOf` reports a source argument outside the target's bound at the spec method** ([#1082](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1082)). A `Gauge<Y extends Number>` reached from a `Node<U>` whose `U` could be anything used to fail in the generated file, where javac refused `Gauge<U>`. Where one bound would do, the message gives the declaration to write. See [Parameterised Targets](../optics/optics_spec_interfaces.md#parameterised-targets).
- **`@InstanceOf` refuses a test that could never match** ([#1091](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1091)). A `Grid<Y> extends Node<Y[]>` reached from a `Node<int[]>` crashed the processor, and is now refused at the spec method. Where the test earns no source type, as a `Box<?>` is no `Node<U>`, the message says no focus would do and offers another class or a spec. See [the message's entry](../optics/compiler_errors.md#instanceof-never-matches).
- **A method named after a Java keyword takes a trailing underscore** ([#1056](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/pull/1056)). An enum constant such as `NEW` or `TRUE`, a sealed subtype named `Default`, an `@EffectAlgebra` permit named `Throw`, or an imported `withDefault` crashed the processor. Their methods are now `new_()`, `true_()`, `default_()` and `throw_()`, and so are `@GenerateErrorEnvelope` factories. See [Prisms](../optics/prisms.md).

---

## Effect Paths {#effect-paths}

### Values that are never null {#never-null}

- **A `Right` or a `Success` always holds a value** ([#1065](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1065)): `Either.right`, `Try.success`, their Path, `EitherT` and `ErrorContext` factories, and `of` on their monads, refuse null, as `Validated` and `EitherOrBoth` already did. A step that succeeds with nothing to return gives `Unit.INSTANCE`, as `VTask.exec` and `Path.ioRunnable` already do. See [Creating Instances](../monads/either_monad.md#creating-instances).
- **A `Left` always holds an error** ([#1077](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1077)): `Either.left`, `EitherT.left`, `raiseError` on `EitherMonad` and `EitherTMonad`, and `Maybe.toEither` refuse null, as every Effect Path has done since 0.4.11. An error with no detail to carry is `Unit.INSTANCE`. See [Creating Instances](../monads/either_monad.md#creating-instances).
- **A lazy computation always gives a value** ([#1078](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1078)): `IO`, `VTask`, `VStream`, `State`, `Lazy`, every other lazy type and their Paths refuse a null value. A value passed in throws at once, and a function that returns null fails the computation when it runs. Only `Id` keeps a null, for the optics. See [A Task Always Gives a Value](../monads/vtask_monad.md#a-task-always-gives-a-value).
- **Every `raiseError` refuses a null error** ([#1078](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1078)): `MonadError.raiseError` takes an error that is never null, so a nullness checker flags `raiseError(null)` on any instance. `Maybe`, `Optional`, `MaybeT` and `OptionalT`, whose failure carries no detail, take `Unit.INSTANCE`. See [The Solution: `raiseError` and `handleErrorWith`](../functional/monad_error.md#the-solution-raiseerror-and-handleerrorwith).
- **`bracketOutcome`'s release sees its error as a `Maybe`** ([#1077](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1077)): release takes an `Either<Maybe<E>, B>`. A typed failure arrives as `Left(Just(e))`, and a failed `onDefect` as `Left(Nothing)`, where it was `Left(null)`. A release lambda that never reads the error needs no change. See [Outcome-aware structured concurrency](../effect/path_vresult.md#outcome-aware-structured-concurrency).
- **The Path SPI answers with an `Optional` where it has nothing to give** ([#1078](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1078)): `PathProvider.monadError()` and `PathRegistry.unregister` return an `Optional`, as `PathRegistry.getProvider` and `GenericPath.monadError()` do, where they returned null. See [PathProvider SPI Registration](../monads/vstream_advanced.md#pathprovider-spi-registration).
- **A deferred trampoline step names a supplier that returns null** ([#1153](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1153), [#1161](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1161)): `Trampoline.defer`, `TrampolinePath.defer` and `Path.trampolineDefer` report `supplier must not return null` when that step runs. The supplier stays lazy.

### Removed after their deprecation {#removed}

- **`StateT` is built from its state function alone** ([#445](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/445)): its constructor, `create` and `StateTKindHelper.stateT` take no `Monad`, and `mapT` takes only the transformation, as on every other transformer. The record holds only that function, so `equals`, `hashCode` and `toString` leave the `Monad` out. See [Running StateT Computations](../transformers/statet_transformer.md#running-statet-computations).
- **`Try` and `TryPath` fold failure first, as `Either` does** ([#452](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/452)): the success-first `fold`, deprecated since 0.4.6, is removed, leaving `foldFailureFirst`. A call to `fold` fails to compile rather than running its two functions the wrong way round. See [Handling Failures](../monads/try_monad.md#handling-failures-foldfailurefirst-recover-recoverwith).
- **Each narrow on `StateTKind` and `KindValidator` has one name** ([#1260](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1260)): `narrowK`, deprecated in 0.4.5, and `narrowWithPattern`, deprecated in 0.4.4, are removed. `StateTKind.narrow` checks the witness at compile time, which `narrowK`'s `Kind<?, A>` parameter did not. `KindValidator.narrowHolder` takes what `narrowWithPattern` took.
- **`@PathConfig` and the `EFFECTFUL` and `ACCUMULATING` capabilities are removed** ([#1262](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1262)): all three were deprecated in 0.4.11 because none did what it said. No processor read `@PathConfig`, and the two capabilities generated what `CHAINABLE` and `RECOVERABLE` do, so nothing generated changes. To rename a Path class, set `suffix` on `@PathSource`. See [Naming and placement](../effect/path_source.md#naming-and-placement).

### Resources, cancellation and concurrency {#resources-and-cancellation}

- **A `VStream` releases its resources when it stops early or fails** ([#1024](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1024)): closing reaches every finaliser upstream that the stream has started reading, through any operator, innermost first. `takeWhile`, `zipWith`, `headOption`, `find` and a failing terminal operation close what they leave unread, so `bracket(...).map(f).headOption()` releases at once. `VStream.closeAfterFailure` closes a failed manual pull. See [onFinalize: Lightweight Cleanup](../monads/vstream_resources.md#onfinalize-lightweight-cleanup).
- **`VStreamReactive` passes cancellation across the bridge** ([#1024](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1024)): a `toPublisher` subscription closes the rest of its stream when it cancels or the stream fails, once it has requested elements. Closing a `fromPublisher` stream cancels its subscription, so `take(n)` stops the publisher. See [Reactive Interop: Flow.Publisher Bridge](../monads/vstream_advanced.md#reactive-interop-flowpublisher-bridge).
- **One `Resource` can serve overlapping uses** ([#1019](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1019)): each `use` releases exactly what it acquired, however the `Resource` was composed. So a `Resource` built once with `map` or `flatMap` and used nested, or once per concurrent request, no longer releases one resource twice and leaks the other. See [Using One Resource Many Times](../monads/vtask_resource.md#using-one-resource-many-times).
- **`bracket`, `guarantee` and `withResource` report a failing cleanup as try-with-resources does** ([#1053](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1053)): when a use fails and its cleanup throws too, the use's exception is reported with the cleanup's suppressed onto it. An exception from `close()` is reported, so a writer whose final flush fails no longer reports success. See [The bracket Pattern](../effect/advanced_topics.md#the-bracket-pattern).
- **A release that blocks finishes after a cancellation** ([#1057](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1057), [#1073](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1073)): it runs with the interrupt status cleared, then restored. That covers a `bracketOutcome` release, a release after a use that caught a cancellation and returned, and each `Saga` compensation. A blocking release, such as a refund, used to fail at once. See [The bracket Pattern](../effect/advanced_topics.md#the-bracket-pattern) and [Saga](../resilience/saga.md#handling-compensation-failures).
- **A `Scope` can run again, be retried, or run on several threads** ([#1052](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1052)): each run of the `VTask` from `join()` opens its own `StructuredTaskScope` with a new `Joiner`. A second run used to see the first run's results, and a retry kept failing with the first attempt's error. `VResultPath.allSucceed` and `firstSuccess` follow. See [Running a Scope Again](../monads/vtask_scope.md#running-a-scope-again).
- **Resilience patterns keep a task's exception and its cancellation** ([#1072](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1072)): `Retry.retryTask`, `Bulkhead.protect` and their Path forms, and `CircuitBreaker.protectWithFallback`, no longer wrap a checked exception, so `retryOn(IOException.class)` retries a task's `IOException`. A cancelled task is not run again or counted by a circuit breaker, and a timeout passes the cancellation on. See [Handling Exhausted Retries](../resilience/retry.md#handling-exhausted-retries).

### Streams, sagas and stack safety {#streams-and-sagas}

- **A `VStream` chunk is a `NonEmptyList`** ([#580](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/580)): `chunk`, `chunkWhile` and `mapChunked`, and `chunk` on `VStreamPath` and `VStreamContext`, hand over a `NonEmptyList`, so `head()`, `reduce` and `max` on a chunk always give a value. `NonEmptyList` gains `stream()`, so a batch function such as `chunk -> chunk.stream().map(f).toList()` compiles unchanged. See [Chunking Operations](../monads/vstream_parallel.md#chunking-operations).
- **A large chunk size or concurrency on a short stream works** ([#1238](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1238), [#1249](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1249)): `chunk(Integer.MAX_VALUE)`, or `parEvalMap` with that concurrency, ran out of memory before reading an element. Each batch list was sized to the argument, and now starts small and grows. The other chunked and parallel calls, and their `VStreamPath` and `VStreamContext` forms, follow. See [Chunking Operations](../monads/vstream_parallel.md#chunking-operations).
- **A saga builder with no steps does not compile** ([#580](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/580)): `SagaBuilder.start()` returns a `SagaBuilder.Start`, which has the step methods but no `build()`. Each step returns a `SagaBuilder` whose `build()` never fails. An empty builder threw `IllegalStateException`. Steps that come from data are held as a `SagaSteps`. See [Steps From Data](../resilience/saga.md#steps-from-data).
- **`TrampolineUtils.traverseListStackSafe` is stack-safe under every applicative** ([#1018](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1018)): it combines the effects as a balanced tree, so a million-element traversal under `IO` no longer overflows the stack. It builds the result in linear time, and a `Validated` collecting its errors in a list is no longer quadratic in the failures. See [Core Components](../monads/trampoline_monad.md#core-components).
- **`@PathSource` points an effect algebra to `FreePath`** ([#1008](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1008)): a Path over a witness that `@EffectAlgebra` generates now draws a note at the witness. The algebra has a `Functor` and no `Monad` to pass to the Path's `of` and `pure`, so the note shows how to wrap its programs in a `FreePath`. See [A witness another processor writes](../effect/path_source.md#a-witness-another-processor-writes).

---

## Spring {#spring}

- **A streamed `VStreamPath` response closes its stream when it stops** ([#1024](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1024)): a client disconnect, a timeout or a serialisation failure now runs the stream's finalisers. See [VStreamPath: SSE Streaming on Virtual Threads](../spring/spring_boot_integration.md#vstreampath-sse-streaming).
- **An SSE stream from a declarative HTTP client closes when you stop early** ([#1024](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1024)): `headOption()`, `find(...)` or `take(n)` on a stream from `HkjClientExchange.vstream` now closes the response. There is no need to drain it first. See [Streaming with `VStreamPath`](../spring/declarative_http_clients.md#streaming-with-vstreampath).
- **An endpoint that sends no body is declared `Unit`** ([#1065](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1065)): a declarative client method returning `EitherPath<E, Unit>`, `VTaskPath<Either<E, Unit>>` or `MaybePath<Unit>` ignores the body. A controller's `Unit` success writes no body from every handler that writes one value. See [Choosing a Return Type](../spring/declarative_http_clients.md#choosing-a-return-type).
- **`hkj-spring` is built against Spring Boot 4.1.1** ([#1177](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1177)): `hkj-spring-boot-autoconfigure` publishes Spring Boot's BOM as a Gradle platform. Gradle then raises the Spring Boot your application runs with, and each library it manages, to at least 4.1.1's versions; a newer requested version still wins. Spring's dependency-management plugin or a Maven BOM import keeps your version, which must be 4.1.0 or later.

---

## Testing {#testing}

- **The lens and affine law harnesses check set-set in both orders** ([#1169](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1169), [#1175](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1175)). The two focus values may be given in either order, and an affine is checked on its present target. The harness is stricter: a fixture that broke set-set only in the order left untested now fails. See [Optic Laws](../tooling/test_assertions.md#optic-laws).
- **Lens and affine law fixtures may include the current focus** ([#812](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/812)). `assertLensLaws` and `assertAffineLaws` require only that their two focus values differ from each other. A boolean lens can use `false, true`. See [Optic Laws](../tooling/test_assertions.md#optic-laws).
- **`assertAffineLaws` law-checks an affine that writes to an absent focus** ([#1023](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/pull/1023)): `Affines.some()` and a `Lens.andThen(Prism)` affine now pass. On the absent target it checks that `modify` changes nothing, that `set` either changes nothing or writes a value that reads back, and set-set. Add `assertSetNoOpWhenAbsent` for an affine that must leave it alone. See [When the focus is absent](../optics/affine.md#when-the-focus-is-absent).
- **The library's own type classes are law-checked more widely** ([#1151](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1151), [#1203](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1203), [#1208](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1208), [#1212](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1212), [#1218](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1218), [#1220](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1220), [#1222](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1222)). The Applicative laws now run for `List`, `NonEmptyList`, `EitherOrBoth` and `Trampoline`, the MonadError laws for `CompletableFuture`, and the Bifunctor laws for `Const` over generated values. The build now fails for a `Monad` with no test class of its own.
- **Showcase tests demonstrate `EitherOrBothAssert` and `NonEmptyListAssert`** ([#1191](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1191)): they join the `hkj-test` examples a reader can copy. Property tests in `hkj-core` and `hkj-checker` share one set of defaults ([#1217](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/pull/1217)).

## Build and tooling {#build-and-tooling}

- **Checker severity settings and the library's formatting work under every default locale** ([#1168](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1168)): `severity=WARNING` and per-check `severity:<id>=WARNING` now select warnings under Turkish, where they were silently ignored. Library formatting and generated identifier case conversions use `Locale.ROOT`. The `hkj-core` and `hkj-examples` tests run under an English locale, with `Locale.ROOT` in more of their formatting ([#1160](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1160), [#1253](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/pull/1253), [#1256](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/pull/1256)).
- **`MigrateDeprecationsTo0_5_0` drops `StateT`'s `Monad` and widens navigated containers** ([#445](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/445), [#1106](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1106)): `RemoveStateTMonadArgument` drops the `Monad` from `StateT` constructor, `create`, `stateT` and `mapT` calls. `AddWidenFieldsForNavigatedContainersRecipe` adds each container a 0.4.x navigator stepped into to `widenFields`, and marks one whose elements have a field named like a path method. See [0.5.0 deprecation migration](../tooling/openrewrite.md#050-deprecation-migration).
- **`MigrateDeprecationsTo0_5_0` marks the nulls to replace** ([#1065](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1065), [#1077](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1077), [#1078](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1078)). `DetectNullSuccessValuesRecipe` and `DetectNullErrorValuesRecipe` mark a `null` given as a success, a value or an error, and a lambda that returns one where it now fails. They also mark `Void` as a value or error type. They rewrite nothing, and `rewriteRun` leaves each mark as a comment. See [0.5.0 deprecation migration](../tooling/openrewrite.md#050-deprecation-migration).
- **`MigrateDeprecationsTo0_6_0` replaces a Focus path's untyped shortcuts** ([#1105](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1105)): the new group's `ReplaceUntypedPathShortcutsRecipe` rewrites each call to its typed form, such as `each()` to `each(EachInstances.listEach())`. It drops a needless type witness, and marks each call it cannot rewrite, such as one over a `List<? extends T>`, with its fix. See [0.6.0 deprecation migration](../tooling/openrewrite.md#060-deprecation-migration).
- **A nullness checker sees every `hkj-core` package as `@NullMarked`** ([#1078](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1078)): `vstream`, `constant`, `func`, `writer_t`, `effect.spi`, `util.validation` and the remaining optics packages carry the package annotation the others already did. NullAway reading `hkj-core` from the classpath ignores the module's annotation, so it treated those types as unannotated.
- **A nullness checker reads `hkj-test`'s assertions** ([#1094](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1094)): its packages carry `@NullMarked`, which NullAway reading the jar from the classpath needs. Every `assertThat...` entry point takes a `@Nullable` actual, as AssertJ's does, so `assertThatEither(result).isNull()` passes for a null `result`, where it threw `NullPointerException`.
- **Some `hkj-test` assertions take or give a null** ([#1094](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1094)): `withMessage`, `withExceptionMessage`, `whenForcedThrowsWithMessage` and `IdAssert.hasValue` take a `@Nullable` expected value. `getException()` and `getValue()` on `IOAssert` and `VTaskAssert` return `@Nullable`, since an outcome has only one of the two.
- **A generator extending the built-in `Optional`, `Maybe`, `List`, `Set` or `Collection` generator inherits no optic expression** ([#757](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/757)): `@GenerateFocus` recognises those types by name and never asks a generator. So `generateOpticExpression()` and `getRequiredImports()` on one return the defaults, and a subclass claiming another type takes no part in `@GenerateFocus` until it names its own. See [Registering your own container type](../optics/focus_containers.md#the-fine-print-registering-your-own-container-type).
- **The `state-t-mapt-arity` check is retired** ([#445](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/445)): every `mapT` now takes the function alone, so there is no missing argument to report. A `disable=` or `severity:` entry that names it has no effect. The `kind-value-narrow` message now names the right accessor: `run()` on `ReaderT` and `WriterT`, and `runStateT(state)` on `StateT`. See [Compile-Time Checks](../tooling/compile_checks.md).
- **`hkj-processor-plugins` no longer brings Guava and Jackson 2 onto your annotation processor path** ([#1177](https://github.com/higher-kinded-j/higher-kinded-j/issues/1177)): they came with `palantir-java-format`, which it declared but never used. The plugin guide's build snippet now names javapoet and the right Avaje SPI artefact. See [Step-by-Step Example](../tooling/generator_plugins.md#step-by-step-example).
